item.title: Atiku slams Tinubu over retired police officers’ pension crisis
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has again accused President Bola Tinubu of abandoning retired police officers to a failing pension system, despite their years of service protecting Nigerians. Atiku said it was unacceptable that officers who risked their lives to keep the country safe now had to stage daily protests at the National Pension Commission, PenCom, to demand the benefits they earned in service. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku described the situation as disgraceful, questioning how a government that deploys police officers to protect the powerful could fail to secure their welfare after retirement. “If police officers who served this country must endure humiliation to demand a fair pension, what hope is there for other Nigerians who have spent their working lives in public service?” he asked. The ADC presidential candidate said he was troubled by the protests and had directed his team to meet with the affected officers to hear their grievances firsthand. He also faulted Tinubu for failing to act on the Police Exit Bill, which, according to the statement, had remained on the President’s desk since March. Atiku accused the administration of treating police officers as expendable, recalling that many spent their careers protecting Nigerians, including political office holders, only to be abandoned when they needed government support most. To address the situation, he said his proposed Police Dignity Guarantee Plan would prioritise the welfare and retirement security of law enforcement personnel through prompt action on the Police Exit Bill, restoration of gratuity for police officers and implementation of the Police Pension Board Bill. “Insecurity cannot be defeated while those who protect the country are denied security in retirement. My Police Dignity Guarantee Plan will ensure that officers who serve Nigeria are properly supported throughout their careers and are not abandoned when they retire,” Atiku said. He pledged to implement the Police Pension Board Bill within 30 days of taking office, adding that his administration would seek to make Nigeria affordable again and restore dignity to those who had devoted their lives to national service. item.title: ‘Give Regina breathing space,’ Ned Nwoko appeals to fans, threatens legal action
item.description: Senator Ned Nwoko has appealed to the public, particularly fans and friends of his estranged wife, Nollywood actress Regina Daniels, to give her space to recover, warning that those spreading false reports about her could face legal action. Nwoko made the appeal in a statement shared on his Instagram page, expressing concern over what he described as the circulation of fabricated death announcements, misleading reports and hurtful content about the actress. He said the appeal was not only for Daniels but also for their children, who, according to him, deserve to see their mother supported and given every opportunity to recover. “I want to make a sincere appeal to the public, particularly Regina’s fans, friends, bloggers and social media commentators, to please give Regina some breathing space,” he said. The senator said Daniels had been through a lot and needed love, support and an opportunity to heal rather than public criticism. “Regina has been through a lot, more than many people may realise, and right now, what she needs most is love, support and the opportunity to recover.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Senator Prince Ned Nwoko (@princenednwoko) He also referenced a video Daniels shared on her birthday, saying it offered a glimpse into some of the health challenges she had been dealing with. According to him, her situation should not be an opportunity for people to judge or vilify her. Nwoko further said her well-being had always been important to him, adding that concerns about her welfare contributed to the decision to bring aspects of their private situation into the public domain. He expressed particular concern over reports falsely announcing the actress’s death and other claims about her health and personal circumstances. “These things are not harmless social media engagement. Regina sees many of these posts, and they are deeply distressing. They do nothing to support her recovery, rather, they add to the burden she is already carrying,” he said. The lawmaker urged the actress’s supporters to discourage the spread of such reports rather than amplify them. He also warned bloggers and social media users against deliberately publishing false information about Daniels, particularly claims concerning her death, health and personal life. “We are documenting these publications, and anyone found responsible will be held accountable through the appropriate legal channels,” he said. Nwoko added that Daniels deserved the opportunity to recover without being subjected to fabricated reports and renewed public scrutiny. item.title: ‘Ongoing dialogue’ with China after Mbappe row – Liga chief Tebas
item.description: La Liga president Javier Tebas said Monday he is maintaining dialogue with Chinese authorities in an effort to defuse a row over Kylian Mbappe’s comments about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV did not air a single La Liga match this weekend, while Real Madrid’s win at Racing Santander on Sunday was also not shown on pay television in the country. In a clip from an interview with French show “The Bridge” which has since been taken down, Mbappe had said he was amused by an internet meme showing his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”, an apparent reference to Mao. Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga apologised for the comment after a backlash in China, where mocking former leader Mao — blamed by historians for millions of deaths — is taboo. “For now, we wait and see how the situation develops… because given how events have unfolded, everything depends on things calming down a bit, on all the mess easing,” Tebas told reporters at the World in Progress forum in Barcelona. “There will be ongoing dialogue — I’m speaking with the Chinese authorities, both in Madrid and in Beijing, and we’re going to wait.” People walk past a bus featuring French football star Kylian Mbappe for Dongpeng Beverage Group’s “Bushuila” electrolyte drink on a street in Shanghai on October 27, 2026. Kylian Mbappe was dropped on October 27 by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football star apparently joked about former leader Mao Zedong. (Photo by Jade GAO / AFP) Tebas, who held a meeting with Chinese ambassador to Spain Yao Jing last week, highlighted several strong links between China and Spanish football which could help resolve the dispute. “We’ve had a strategy for several years now with the political and sporting authorities in China,” he explained. Tebas met Chinese State Councillor Shen Yiqin and a high-ranking delegation at Barcelona’s La Masia youth academy facilities in February, along with Barcelona president Joan Laporta. “With the president of China Media Group (the parent organisation of CCTV) we have a good agreement,” continued Tebas. “He’s been to La Liga, I’ve met with him (Shen Haixiong). Every time I travel to Beijing I have a meeting with him.” China effectively cut ties with the NBA for several years from 2019 after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted his support for Hong Kong protesters, but Tebas said he was “hopeful” of reverting the current situation. “I’m going to travel, talk, and keep talking with the Chinese authorities,” he added. “We’ll try everything possible to normalise the situation as much as we can.” Mbappe scored on Sunday as Real Madrid beat Racing 3-0 in La Liga to move within three points of leaders Barcelona. item.title: NASS committed to increasing women’s participation — Bamidele
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, has said the 10th National Assembly is committed to removing barriers limiting women’s participation in governance through a proposed constitutional amendment seeking special seats for women in the National and State Houses of Assembly. Bamidele, who represents Ekiti Central Senatorial District, said the proposed legislation was designed to address the persistent under-representation of women in Nigeria’s political institutions and ensure their participation in decisions affecting the country. He spoke as a guest speaker at the 2026 Law Week of the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Ekiti State Chapter, held in Ado-Ekiti, with the theme, “Justice in a Changing World: Responding to New Challenges Affecting Women and Children”. The Senate Leader said the proposed constitutional alteration would create 37 additional seats in the Senate and 37 in the House of Representatives, with one seat reserved for women in each state and the Federal Capital Territory. He added that the proposal also provided for three additional seats in each State House of Assembly, without displacing existing legislative seats. According to him, the arrangement is proposed to run for 16 years, covering four electoral cycles, after which its impact would be reviewed. Describing the initiative as a historic intervention rather than a partisan project, Bamidele said a democracy that excluded a significant proportion of its population from decision-making could not claim to be fully representative. He disclosed that the National Assembly had commenced engagements with State Houses of Assembly to secure the constitutionally required concurrence for the proposed amendment. He said the process was being pursued through extensive consultations and consensus-building. Bamidele, who commended the advocacy of the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, said the 10th Assembly was determined to address historical gaps in women’s political representation. The lawmaker also identified globalisation, artificial intelligence, digitalisation, insecurity, economic instability and climate change as factors creating new challenges for women and children. He said women continued to face gender-based violence, economic exclusion, discrimination and inadequate healthcare, while children remained vulnerable to sexual abuse, trafficking, child labour, early marriage, malnutrition, educational deprivation and digital exploitation. He noted that poverty, unemployment, inadequate social protection, educational inequalities, social stigma and weak enforcement of existing laws had further compounded the challenges. Bamidele maintained that protecting women and children was not merely a humanitarian responsibility but a constitutional obligation and a critical investment in national development, economic productivity and social stability. item.title: NASS proposes 74 additional seats for women
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The National Assembly Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution has proposed the creation of 74 additional seats for women in the Senate and House of Representatives, Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, has said. The proposal also provides for three additional seats reserved for women in each State House of Assembly, without displacing any existing seats. Bamidele, who represents Ekiti Central Senatorial District, disclosed this on Monday at the 2026 Law Week organised by the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Ekiti State Chapter. He said the proposals were aimed at deepening women’s participation and representation in Nigeria’s political and governance processes. The programme, organised by the Ekiti State chapter of FIDA, chaired by Mrs Ayobami Olowoyo-Richards, had the theme, “Justice in a Changing World: Responding to New Challenges Affecting Women and Children.” In a statement issued by his Media Directorate, Bamidele, who is also Vice Chairman of the Senate Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution, said the proposed special seats were part of the ongoing constitutional amendment process. He said: “A Bill for an Act to alter the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to provide for special seats for women in the National and State Houses of Assembly and for related matters is receiving our attention at the National Assembly.” Explaining the proposal, the Senate Leader said it would create 37 additional seats in the Senate and another 37 in the House of Representatives. According to him, if approved, each state of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory will have one additional seat in each chamber of the National Assembly. He said the committee had also proposed three additional seats for women in each State House of Assembly. Bamidele said the arrangement was designed to operate for 16 years, covering four electoral cycles, after which it would be subjected to a comprehensive review. He described the proposed duration as a sunset clause intended to allow the development of a more inclusive political culture. He said the committee was engaging with state Houses of Assembly, whose concurrence was constitutionally required for the proposed amendment to take effect. Bamidele said the initiative was not partisan but aimed at addressing the under-representation of women in decision-making. He added that the 10th National Assembly’s commitment to the proposal had been strengthened by advocacy from key government figures, including the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. On the broader protection of women and children, Bamidele said laws must respond to emerging threats and ensure that victims of abuse had access to protection and justice. He said justice should be accessible, affordable, timely and effective, adding that women experiencing domestic violence and children subjected to abuse must be protected from intimidation and further harm. item.title: Tinubu concludes Saudi Arabia visit after Umrah
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has concluded his visit to Saudi Arabia, where he performed the Umrah pilgrimage and entered the Holy Kaaba to pray. Tinubu, who departed Abuja last Thursday, announced the conclusion of his visit on Monday in a post on his X account. The President was accompanied on the trip by some state governors, members of the business community and cabinet ministers. In the post, Tinubu said he and members of his delegation had the rare privilege of entering the Holy Kaaba to pray and performing Umrah. He expressed gratitude to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and the Crown Prince and Prime Minister, Mohammed bin Salman, for granting them the privilege and extending hospitality to the delegation. He said the visit reflected the longstanding bonds of faith and friendship between Nigeria and Saudi Arabia. Tinubu added that he used the opportunity to pray for peace, unity and prosperity for Nigeria and its citizens. item.title: FCT police arrest two suspected cable vandals in Guzape
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Operatives of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command have arrested two suspected members of a cable vandalism gang and recovered several cut-to-size armoured cables in Guzape, Abuja. The command’s spokesperson, SP Josephine Adeh, disclosed this on Monday, saying the arrests followed a routine surveillance patrol along Walter Ofonagoro Street, Guzape, in the early hours of October 31, 2026. Adeh said police operatives attached to Guzape Division, at about 1:30am, sighted a Lexus SUV and a Toyota Sienna parked under suspicious circumstances. She said the operatives approached the vehicles to ascertain the occupants’ reasons for being at the location, but the occupants sped off on sighting the police team, abandoning an accomplice who attempted to escape on foot. According to her, the operatives gave chase, intercepted and arrested the suspect. Preliminary investigations identified him as Sagir Abubakar of Kuchigoro Village, FCT, and allegedly linked him to a gang that targets secluded locations within the territory to vandalise public and private infrastructure. Adeh said a search of the surrounding premises where the suspects had been sighted led to the recovery of several armoured cables cut into pieces. She added that further investigations led to the arrest of another suspected accomplice, identified as Seidu Umar Bello, who had initially escaped in one of the vehicles. The police spokesperson said investigations were ongoing to establish the full extent of the suspects’ activities, identify other members of the gang and apprehend those still at large. She said the two suspects remained in custody and would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations. The command urged residents to remain vigilant and report suspicious persons or activities to the nearest police station or through its emergency lines: 08032003913 and 08061581938. item.description: *’Ajaero doesn’t understand Labour negotiations,’ Osifo retorts By Victor Ahiuma-Young & Kafayat Kokumo The rift between the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, has deepened following fresh accusations by NLC President, Joe Ajaero, that his TUC counterpart, Festus Osifo, is undermining the collective struggle of Nigerian workers. Read Also: 2027: Obi couldn’t fix Anambra; Atiku will return to Dubai after election — Oshiomhole Ajaero made the remarks on Monday during an interview on Channels TV’s ‘The Morning Brief’. He defended the NLC’s handling of the controversial N70, 000 transport allowance secured from the Federal Government, insisting that the agreement was the product of collective bargaining and not a unilateral arrangement by the NLC. He also dismissed allegations that he was not a team player, declaring that the disagreements between the two labour centres should be examined based on facts rather than personal sentiments. The NLC President further questioned the TUC leadership’s commitment to workers’ interests, challenging its president over his alleged absence from Nigeria and the whereabouts of buses allocated to the organisation under the government’s compressed natural gas, CNG, transportation initiative. Usifo reacts In a swift reaction, President of TUC, Festus Osifo, disagreed with the stance of Joe Ajaero, maintaining, among others, that the NLC cannot negotiate the salaries and allowances of TUC members in the public service. However, speaking on the controversy surrounding the N70,000 transport allowance, Ajaero insisted that the agreement was negotiated with the Federal Government following an ultimatum issued by organised labour over the rising cost of living. He said the meeting that produced the agreement was attended by representatives of the Ministry of Labour, the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, the Budget Office, the Ministry of Finance and the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation. According to him, the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council was also represented at the meeting, with its secretary signing the agreement on behalf of the council. Ajaero said: “We issued an ultimatum to the government and were preparing to embark on industrial action. The government requested four days to meet with us at the Presidential Villa. “Following that meeting, agreements were reached.Every collective bargaining process produces an agreement. In this instance, the N70,000 transport allowance was included in the agreement. “I, therefore, do not understand the argument that the government simply gave us the money without any negotiation.” He further argued that the negotiating council had eight unions on its trade union side, seven affiliated with the NLC and one with the TUC, insisting that the presence and participation of the council’s representatives validated the agreement. item.title: Tinubu concludes Saudi Arabia visit, says he prayed for Nigeria
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has concluded his visit to Saudi Arabia, where he performed the lesser Hajj, known as Umrah, and entered the Holy Kaaba to offer prayers. Tinubu disclosed this in a statement following the visit, expressing gratitude to Saudi Arabia’s King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman for granting him and members of his delegation the privilege. The President also appreciated the Saudi leadership for its hospitality and support, describing the gesture as a reflection of the longstanding relationship between Nigeria and the Kingdom. He said he used the opportunity to pray for peace, unity and prosperity in Nigeria. “I have concluded my visit to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, where, together with members of my delegation, I had the rare honour of entering the Holy Kaaba to pray, and of performing Umrah. “I am deeply grateful to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and to Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman for extending this privilege to us, and for their gracious hospitality and brotherly care. It reflects the enduring bonds of faith and friendship between Nigeria and Saudi Arabia. “In those sacred moments, I prayed for peace, unity and prosperity for our dear nation and for all Nigerians,” He wrote. item.title: Sokoto SSANU begins warning strike over unpaid entitlements
item.description: ….Union threatens indefinite shutdown if demands remain unmet By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), Sokoto State University (SSU) chapter, has commenced a five-working-day warning strike over outstanding staff entitlements, threatening an indefinite shutdown if the dispute with the Sokoto State Government is not resolved. The union said the industrial action followed the expiration of a 14-working-day ultimatum issued to the state government over its demands. In a statement signed by its Chairman, Ismail Bala Muhammed, and Secretary, Mansur Ahmad, SSANU said the strike was triggered by the government’s failure to approve and implement the outstanding entitlements despite repeated engagements. The association said it initially submitted its demands through the appropriate channels before forwarding a comprehensive document on July 28, 2026, following the agreement between the Federal Government and the union on the 35 per cent Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance (CONTTA). It said it subsequently made several verbal and written appeals, including visits to the Commissioner for Higher Education, the Permanent Secretary of the ministry and the Deputy Governor, in a bid to secure an amicable settlement. Following the engagements, the state government constituted a committee comprising the Commissioner for Higher Education, the Permanent Secretary, the Deputy Accountant-General and Professor Mustapha Aliyu to engage representatives of SSANU, the National Association of Academic Technologists (NAAT) and the Non-Academic Staff Union (NASU) from SSU and Shehu Shagari University of Education. At a meeting on October 9, the government communicated its position on the outstanding claims. However, SSANU said the response failed to address its members’ major concerns. According to the union, the government rejected payment of arrears arising from the 25 per cent salary increment, proposed implementing CONTTA from January 2027 subject to budgetary provision, and maintained that annual salary increments had already been implemented. Dissatisfied with the outcome, SSANU said it convened an emergency congress on October 13, where members resolved to issue a 14-working-day ultimatum to the government. The union warned that failure to meet its demands would trigger a five-day warning strike and potentially an indefinite industrial action. It, however, temporarily suspended the planned announcement of the strike after the Permanent Secretary scheduled a meeting with representatives of SSANU from SSU and Shehu Shagari University of Education on October 14. item.title: Otti: Abia won’t celebrate thieves, drug barons again
item.description: …Governor honours Emeritus Professor Oluikpe at 90 By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has said his administration is working to dismantle what he described as a culture of celebrating thieves, fraudsters, drug barons and other questionable characters, insisting that public recognition should be reserved for people of integrity and genuine accomplishments. Otti spoke at the 90th birthday celebration of Emeritus Professor Benson Oluikpe in Umuahia, where he said his administration was institutionalising the celebration of excellence to inspire younger generations to pursue worthy achievements. “We want to depart from that inherited culture. It’s not our culture. Culture of celebrating thieves. Culture of celebrating 419-ers. Culture of celebrating drug barons. Culture of celebrating bandits. That’s not our culture. That’s not how we grew up,” the governor said. He faulted the practice of honouring outstanding individuals only after their death, when they could no longer enjoy the recognition, saying achievers should be celebrated while alive. According to him, recognising people for their contributions would encourage others, particularly young people, to aspire to excellence. Otti cited the recent celebration of five Abia schoolchildren who emerged champions at an international competition in Qatar, saying his administration was determined to make excellence, rather than questionable wealth and influence, the basis for public recognition. The governor also used a personal experience to illustrate the importance of accountability, recalling how his father questioned him in 1989 over the source of the N100 he sent home while working at Citibank. He said he had earned the money through extra work and daily allowances, but his father insisted on knowing how he legitimately made it. “That’s how I was brought up. You needed to give account. But these days, people don’t ask questions. We need to go back to that time when we would ask questions. Ask your children questions. Let them give account,” he said. Otti maintained that people’s values, rather than the times, had changed, citing his son’s decision to provide receipts and explanations for money he had saved towards buying a house in the United States. Earlier, Oluikpe expressed gratitude for the honour and prayed for God’s blessings on the governor. “You have honoured me; may God honour you,” the nonagenarian said. The professor, who disclosed that he first met Otti in 2013 when the governor was still a banker, described him as a humble man endowed with wisdom. He said the impression he formed of Otti during their first encounter influenced his subsequent support for the governor’s political ambition. Recounting how Otti once stood up to return an award to him at a public function, Oluikpe said the gesture demonstrated a humility that had remained consistent in the governor’s public life. item.title: 2027: Niger Delta Youths slam Uzodinma’s aide over attack on Wike
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA -A political group,Niger Delta Youth Movement, NDYM, has warned an aide to Governor Hope Uzodinma,Mr. Collins Opurozor,to stop attacking the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory,FCT, Nyesom Wike over the senatorial tussle between the Governor and Owelle Rochas Okorocha. The group also urged Opurozor not to use the disagreement between the two APC Chieftains to create hostility between the South East zone and Wike. The group alleged that Opurozor has been attempting to undermine Wike through inflammatory political remarks. The Movement declared that it would not continue to watch Opurozor attack the FCT Minister without consequences and urged him to exercise restraint and desist from using media interviews to settle political scores. In a statement by its Publicity Secretary, Comrade Jeffery Nwali, NDYM condemned Opurozor’s comments on a national television where he accused Wike of attempting to turn the South East into his personal political fiefdom by allegedly encouraging the emergence of weak leaders in the region to preserve his political influence. Describing the comments as reckless and provocative,the group,however, insisted that Wike’s political engagements should not be misrepresented as an attack on Igbo interests. The statement read;”We condemn the attempt by Collins Opurozor to drag the FCT Minister into Imo State’s political disputes, particularly following the Federal High Court judgment concerning Governor Uzodinma’s APC senatorial candidacy in Imo West senatorial zone. “Disagreements between Uzodinma and other political actors in Imo State should not be allowed to create unnecessary hostility between the South East and the FCT Minister. “During the television interview, Opurozor strongly criticized the judgment, dismissed Senator Samuel Anyanwu over what he described as his lack of grassroots support in Imo State, and berated the administration of former Governor Rochas Okorocha as too disgraceful to be remembered. “He also accused Wike of undermining Igbo political interests by allegedly supporting political figures opposed to Uzodinma. “Collins Opurozor is a young political aide who over- rates his intelligence and mistakes verbal aggression for political sophistication. item.title: Nigeria targets wider access to West African markets
item.description: … FG urges businesses to exploit ECOWAS trade scheme By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja LOKOJA — The Federal Government has urged Nigerian manufacturers, farmers and entrepreneurs to take advantage of the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme (ETLS) to expand their businesses into West African markets. The government said increased regional trade was critical to economic growth, integration and stability across the sub-region. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, made the call at the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme Sensitisation Workshop for the North-Central zone, held in Lokoja, Kogi State, in collaboration with the ECOWAS Commission. Enikanolaiye disclosed that Nigeria had registered about 3,500 companies and 20,000 products under the scheme, but said the figures remained below the country’s potential compared with the performance of some other ECOWAS member states. He urged Nigerian businesses to exploit the scheme, which grants qualifying products originating from member countries preferential access to regional markets, to increase exports, expand production and improve the country’s competitiveness. The minister identified the agricultural potential of Kogi and other North-Central states as an opportunity to develop products for regional and international markets. He listed livestock, mangoes, millet, maize, sugar, groundnuts and cashew as commodities that could be processed into value-added products for export to other West African countries. Enikanolaiye urged participants to use the workshop to familiarise themselves with product registration procedures, rules of origin, certification and other requirements for accessing preferential markets under the scheme. “Expanding trade among African countries would not only promote economic cooperation but also strengthen relationships among nations and contribute to peace and security across the continent,” he said. The minister’s appeal comes as Kogi State seeks to position itself as a centre for regional commerce, industrial production and agricultural processing, leveraging its geographical location and natural resources. Welcoming participants, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo said the state’s location at the confluence of Rivers Niger and Benue, agricultural resources, solid mineral deposits and road networks connecting major economic centres offered significant opportunities for trade and investment. Ododo said his administration’s 32-year development plan was designed to translate these advantages into sustainable economic prosperity. He disclosed that the proposed Ajaokuta Free Trade Zone, Agro-Processing Zone and Kogi International Airport were among the strategic projects being pursued to attract investors, expand production capacity and connect local businesses to international markets. item.title: How I met my wife 22 years ago – Actor Odunlade Adekola
item.description: Nollywood actor Odunlade Adekola has celebrated his wife, Ruth Abosede Adekola, on her birthday, recalling how he approached her and expressed his intention to marry her about 22 years ago. The 49-year-old actor shared the tribute in an Instagram post on Monday, reflecting on the beginning of their relationship and his decision to make her his wife. “I saw Madam Ruth Abosede Adekola about 22 years ago!” he wrote. “I walked up to her and said, ‘My friend! I see what I want in you. Can you be mine?’” Adekola, who described Ruth as the mother of his children, also recalled getting fully engaged to her two decades ago. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Odunlade Adekola (@odunomoadekola) “20 years ago, I got fully engaged to my baby, the MOTHER of our KINGS. Deaconess Ruth Abosede Adekola,” he added. The actor further described his wife as his “number one fan”, reaffirming his love and commitment to her while promising to cherish her for the rest of his life. He also offered prayers for God’s continued favour upon their household, wished her a happy birthday and urged his followers to join him in celebrating her. Adekola, over the years, has established himself in Nollywood as an actor, screenwriter, film producer and director. item.title: Ogun 2027: Adebutu dismisses exclusion from INEC list
item.description: ……receives over 1,000 APC defectors into PDP in Ogun By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has dismissed the omission of his name from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) list of governorship candidates as a temporary distraction, insisting that the development would not derail his ambition to contest the 2027 governorship election. Adebutu spoke on Monday while receiving more than 1,000 defectors from the All Progressives Congress (APC) into the PDP at the party’s State Secretariat in Abeokuta, the Ogun State capital. The defectors, led by a former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Segun William, were received by Adebutu alongside prominent PDP leaders, including the party’s Ogun Central senatorial candidate, Iyabo Obasanjo. Addressing the gathering, Adebutu expressed confidence that the controversy surrounding his omission from INEC’s list would eventually be resolved, maintaining that he remained a bona fide member of the PDP. He argued that his political history and participation in elections under the party’s platform over the past two decades were sufficient evidence of his loyalty, challenging those questioning his membership to produce evidence of when he allegedly defected. “I have been the candidate of the PDP for the last 20 years, in every election cycle. My question is: at what stage did I leave or vacate the party? Where is the proof that, for one day, I have even visited the APC office, let alone joined the party?” he asked. The PDP chieftain further disclosed that he played an active role in organising and financing the party’s recent membership registration exercise in Ogun State, which, according to him, recorded more than 19,800 members. He said his registration number in the exercise was 1536, describing the development as further evidence of his continued membership of the opposition party. Adebutu alleged that the controversy surrounding his name on the INEC list was an attempt to distract the opposition and disenfranchise voters, but assured party supporters that the PDP would remain focused on its political activities. “The controversy surrounding my name on the INEC list is an attempt to distract the opposition and disenfranchise voters. But I assure our supporters that this party will not lose focus,” he said. He also disclosed that the party had intensified its grassroots mobilisation across the state, revealing that its campaign team had visited 12 of Ogun State’s 20 local government areas and more than 140 of the 236 wards. item.title: 2027: 42 trade unions in Delta back Tinubu, Oborevwori, Dafinone
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — AHEAD of the January 16, elections, a coalition of 42 trade unions in Delta State has pledged support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎The coalition, operating under the Delta State Informal Sector Association, comprises over 120,000 artisans and informal sector workers across the state. ‎ ‎The group pledged its allegiance at the weekend when its leadership paid a solidarity visit to Senator representing Delta Central Senatorial District, Ede Dafinone. ‎ ‎While receiving the representatives of the association, Senator Dafinone described their coming together under one platform as a significant step towards strengthening grassroots mobilisation and political engagement. ‎ ‎He commended the various trade unions for uniting under the association and appreciated them for reaffirming their support for Tinubu, Oborevwori, his own re-election and the success of all APC candidates in the 2027 elections. ‎ ‎The senator said “this development reflects a shared commitment to strengthening our party’s political structures through effective grassroots mobilisation and sustained engagement with different segments of society.” ‎ ‎He also acknowledged the importance of the informal sector, noting that the coalition’s broad membership provided an avenue for deeper engagement with artisans, traders and other workers across Delta State.
